analysis.name: Andrea Bierema
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bierema is kind and clearly cares about the wellbeing of her students. She's easy to reach out to and gives lots of reminders about due dates and homework. D2L-wise, this is the most organized class I've ever had. There is a lot of work in this class, but it's super easy and Bierema is an easy grader.  Show up to class, look at the checklist, easy.

She's caring and stuff but she explains things so confusingly. It could be the most straight forward assignment and somehow everyone is confused because she used 10 pages to explain it. Even the syllabus is SEVENTY THREE pages long. She literally confuses everyone. Even though I got a good grade I felt like I was going insane reading instructions

She's a good professor, but for being a half-online class, it is the most work I have ever done. It's just busy work, but it gets annoying doing it every week. It's all group work, so it's not that difficult in class. If you miss class, you have to do alternative work, which is much harder than the in-person work, so you should just show up.

She is decent. I personally never had a love for the topic so I didn't find the class that enteraining.
Its all group work so being in class is a must you get 3 skips for the semester
The group work isnt bad its just sometimes annoying to do when you have alot of other schoolwork to do
Mostly it is in class work though, final needs is done outside

Professor Bierema is a very nice lady, but I genuinely would not recommend taking this class in person if it is a requirement. Her D2L is terribly organized and the instructions for assignments are overwhelming. No examples are given, and she generally gives overly detailed explanations that make understanding worse. Not content.

analysis.name: JeanaDee Allen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She treats students like children and does not care about them, uses jingles to get their attention and does pointless exercises that actually stifle creativity. She tries to be all sunshine and roses but you can tell she doesn't want to be there because she is treating it like free association. One of the worst classes I have ever been in.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. The hw is not difficult, but it is EXTREMELY time consuming. It's only 2 hours, but it somehow manages to feel like the longest 2 hours of your life. The students are often treated like children; with name tags and jinglebells to get our attention. If I can save one poor soul from this class, then my mission is complete.

Probably one of the most lackluster classes I have ever taken. I have no idea how this syllabus has been approved. It is all over the place and the professor talks about being progressive but does not offer accommodations if you experience an emergency. Truly performative in the lectures and in practice.

I really liked Professor Allen. She has a wonderful personality and seems to care about student's well-being. She also cares about the deeper meaning behind what she teaches. Class work is a lot, but if you set some time aside to do the work, read instructions, and ask questions, this class is an easy A.
JeanaDee Allen means well, but for a level 100 class I do more work in some of my 300/400 combine. If at all take another CAS class.

analysis.name: Andrea Garmyn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The topics is interesting, but the quality of instruction is fairly poor. The exams are incredibly difficult and not much help from the provided study guide. The instructors only read off the slides and expect us to know what's happening when we evaluate in the barns. Would not recommend the class if you don't have to take it.

Dr Garmyn is a fun professor and for FSC433 there are a lot of lectures and ton of content, but the labs make it fun. The final group project is graded on if you put in work and learned something rather than how well it turned out. Exams are long, but manageable if you study. She is very relaxed with grading and looks for effort over correctness.

Haven't finished the class yet, but professor Garmyn is great for an easy 3.5-4.0 class to boost your GPA! While the only thing I disliked was that she didn't answer or take questions till after class, whatever thought you wanted to ask, save it till the end. Reads off Powerpoint slides, exams are easy, same for homework and quizzes, Iclicker grade

She was decent. Her lectures mainly consisted of her reading off of lecture slides the whole time but at least the class was short. Homework is graded off completion and quizzes are questions right from the homework so that wasn't too bad. Exams are a bit hard but if you study the homework and quizzes it isn't awful. Overall an okay professor.

Most boring prof Ive ever had. Attendance is mandatory, because if it werent people wouldnt bother to show up. The whole class period is her reading off PowerPoint slides. Every Day. Three times a week. For the whole semester. The class itself isnt very difficult but unless you REALLY care about meat, dont plan staying awake in this class.

analysis.name: Amber Peters
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: To be honest her class is pretty easy. There are in class questions you must answer for attendance/grade, but class material is pretty easy. Exams are half multiple choice half written but again not hard. She is gone doing research a lot so will have canceled classes/ TA ran classes which is nice. My downfall was not paying attention in class

Dr. Peters is super nice! She taught half of the lectures, and Dr. Peacor taught the other half. I think that she had simpler topics, so it was easier to understand her. The rest of the class was quite difficult outside of her lectures. Something that made things a bit difficult was her lack of study materials for exams.

Dr. Peters is a great professor! She obviously knows what she's talking about and welcomes any questions or comments on the material. She makes an effort to get to know the class and lectures are engaging and interesting. Attendance is not required but participation matters! Exams are written response but easy if you go to class and participate.

I loved Dr. Peters! I enjoyed taking her Great Lakes Bio class. It wasn't a ton of work and the quizzes felt fair. This semester, she offered that if you had over a 90% in the class you didn't have to take the final exam so make sure you attend class! There were no attendance drops but a few chances for extra credit.

Dr. Peters is a good professor and she is obviously very knowledgeable in her field. However, her grading is weird sometimes and her quizzes/tests are all short answer. I would take her class again, but be prepared for it to be slightly unorganized and for her to be gone several lectures.

analysis.name: Casim Abbas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely loved him, he's very nice and helpful. He will stop lecture and explain everything if you missed something, and if you get a chance to talk to him after/outside of class, he is super helpful and very nice. Would definitely recommend and if I could, I would have him teach all of my math courses!

I love Abbas, his lectures are thorough and well explained. Even if you don't like his lectures, you can always not attend lectures and instead watch videos on D2L from professor Maccombs, who is also an amazing professor. Overall the class is difficult but you have many options on how you want to approach the material.

Not the best professor you can have for Calc 3, but he is very good, thoroughly explains the content and goes step by step to complete complex problems. If you go to his lectures without fail and understand the concepts, you're gonna succeed in his class.

Similar to the majority of my peers, I quickly stopped attending Calculus II lectures. Instead I watched the videos/self taught. His accent, handwriting, and lecture pacing made in person lectures difficult to comprehend. Quizzes are weekly and can be difficult. MTH 133 is a rigorous course, the average final exam grade this semester was a 43% GLHF

A lot of people complain about his lectures but I actually found them very useful and digestible. I understand peoples' complaints but his lecture style reflects "different strokes for different folks." He goes through the theorems and concepts very quickly, but he provides many examples after which I find more helpful. Take notes and go to lecture

analysis.name: Ani Sarkissian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is a 300-level course, which is upper-level in the PLS department, so expect a lot of reading (4 texts) and writing. Prof. Sarkissian is great, but you cannot wing this class. This is a discussion-based course, so you are expected to participate. There is a participation grade, discussion posts, three essay exams, and a book report.

Tough test grader despite simple material. Does Iclicker quizzes with lots of dumb/poorly worded/trick questions. Only missed 1-2 classes the whole semester but got a 75% attendance grade because the clicker quizzes were so dumb. Not an unbearable class but frustrating at times.

4 Exams, lowest is dropped and the other points come from participation points that come from attending lectures, answering pop questions via iclicker, easy enough if you do the reading and pay minimal attention to lecture. Issue is in the exams, multi-choice questions feel completely random, rubric for essay is there but not applied to grading.

Professor Sarkissian is extremely knowledgeable about political science. The course itself is pretty straightforward but exam questions can be tricky sometimes. I really enjoyed this class and I appreciate her answering my questions on politics inside and outside the class. Participation portion is easy to achieve points. No extra credit options.

Extremely hard grader on exams, homework, and even in-class participation. Hours of homework per night. Lectures are based solely on homework discussion questions, isn't really teaching you anything, just talking about the book. Very blunt, says she doesn't understand your thinking and doesn't offer any suggestions to do better. Wouldn't recommend.

analysis.name: Ayoob Bazgir
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 104 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This professor has the ability to simplify complex topics so students can understand and truly cares about the success of students. The practice problems and quizzes matched perfectly with the exams, and there were never any surprises. I took this class accelerated in 6 weeks instead of 16 and it was an easy 4.0.

Take Ayoob for orgo, and nobody else. his 8am lectures both semesters are the only 8am classes I've ever taken, only because I actually loved the class. Orgo is notoriously a weeder class but NOT Ayoobs class. You will learn the material so well and enjoy it. This might be a hot take but general chem was harder than his classes. Take his class!

He makes chemistry so easy with his comparisons to real-world analysis. He truly wants all his students to see how complex concepts can be broken down in simple ways. He allows students to engage during lectures free of shame. He makes funny jokes and does call-and-responses so we all stay engaged. 10% EC boost to your grade. Everyone loves him

I was super scared to take orgo, but Ayoob made it so easy. He explains everything clearly and reviews past content at the beginning of lectures. 8am lectures with attendance not required, but I still went.  Activ takes a while to get the hang of, but there's also 10% (or more) extra credit offered. Needed 24% on the final to 4.0. Highly recommend!

Great prof, lots of opportunities for extra credits, I got a OK Exams and quizzes but bcs I did all the hws and extra credits, which you got tons of time for btw, and I got a 4.0. If you miss his lectures, the video lecture are still great and they are not too long. Most lectures he also lets you leave early which is great. great prof, good man.

analysis.name: Adolfo Ausin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst professor I have had here at MSU. The class itself is okay, it's graded pretty tough. However as a professor he lacks empathy and understanding for students. You only get two absences for the entire semester despite having excuses absences, doctors notes, going to competitions for clubs, etc.

Basically this course is taught by like random teachers that answer to Professor Ausin, he's not involved like whatsoever he just does the grading and posts the assignments but he's not there for the actual in person class. Lots of homework every week and very heavy lecture material.

I had professor Ausin for SPN 440. It's not listed here so I wasn't able to choose it, but this professor is awful. The class was online asynchronous but with weekly check-ins. However, Prof Ausin felt so uninvolved and gave terrible feedback. Exams are all oral, and he gives only 18 minutes for 36-question quizzes. I felt set up for failure.

He is extremely uninvolved with the class. He does online, recorded lectures that are terrible. This is my 7th year taking Spanish, I received a 4 on the AP Spanish exam, so I already know the topics being taught. In my opinion, they're taught horribly. Along with that, the tests/quizzes set you up for failure with strange, unnecessary specifics.

Terribly structured class. He takes over 60 slides to explain a topic that our in class professors can explain in 6. I wish I could attach a photo to this review to help you visualize how crowded and confusing  the slides unnecessarily are. He uses grammar structures to explain themself, harder if you aren't familiar with concepts already.

analysis.name: Brittany Busby
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In theory, this class was perfect. However, the lack of documentation and instruction from the professors to the TAs made it very disorganized. TAs were looking for things that were not mentioned in resources. Also, the course provided no template or format for how reports were to be formatted. TAs were very nice though, and made class enjoyable.

This lab was excruciating. The TA's have no idea what they're doing and are very unhelpful in answering questions. The projects have so much pointless writing that is expected to be done 1-2 days after lab. The grading really isn't very harsh, I found that throwing a bunch of words on a page will get you 100% pretty easily. It's a lot of work.

Hope you get good TA's bc your experience is dependent on them. Some are tough graders others are chill. Way too much work for a 1 credit class, need a good group or to be able to do all the work yourself. Prof was not present in any way. Labs were weird (have to design yourself & takes a while) but fun. Can't leave early even if ur done. Decent.

TAs and ULA will actually teach this class so I guess it depends more on them, but this class isn't super hard to do well in but it is SO boring. And if you get a bad group then youre cooked. I reccommend if you do not do well with your group, complain in the CATME surveys and they will likely change your group and label is as a "attendance change"

CEM 161 is not actually taught by Dr. Busby herself, but is instead taught by 2 TA's chose at random. Your grade in this class will likely depend on what 2 TA's you get and what 3 group members you get. Group members are chose at random. CEM 161 wasn't extremely difficult but does require a decent amount of effort and some knowledge from CEM 141.

analysis.name: Sue Allen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 191 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Poor teaching style. Talks too much before class then rushes at the end, overall not organized in the slightest (which I need in a professor) her explanations are not cohesive/helpful. Treated class like high school, she's very funny but not a good math professor fit, she should be a highschool history teacher! If you're bad at math don't take her.

I didn't enjoy professor Allen's teaching style. She treated the class like a highschool class, and showed us the same sort of respect as highschoolers. She tends to start talking way before class started and usually ended class late. She was also sensitive about people leaving early. She was fine, but I didn't love her teaching style or anything.

such a difficult professor, so much to do on webwork but she says its not important. You only learn in lecture (not recitation), so if you miss the lecture or part of the lecture you're done for. She won't answer questions that she answered in class already, which made it feel like you couldn't email her with questions, also won't reteach concepts.

She's a great teacher. I am terrible at math but I still managed a 3.0. I suggest attending all lectures and taking notes. Do webwork the same day as the lecture so it is easier. If you struggle GO TO OFFICE HOURS or MLC! She will help you with your homework and with your grades. She gives practice problems that aren't due, but really help.

If you're good at math do other students a favor and take her lecture (people not good at math will struggle with her teaching style so let them take a better prof.) Lectures are too short for the amount of chatting she does. I retaught myself content after class. She's sweet and wants to help you when 1-on-1 but she should teach a smaller class.

analysis.name: Cristina Bodea
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really liked her as a professor and enjoyed most of the content, however there was just so much work to where I felt like I was not genuinely learning anything. I felt like I was just trying to do the bare minimum because I have 10 other assignments to do for the course. I would recommend shortening the workload as it was A LOT

Professor Bodea is kind and knowledgable. She cares deeply about all of her students which would be evident to aynone who attends her office hours. She outlines the course clearly in the syllabus and just like with any other class you must study to earn a good grade. Her lectures are interesting and thoughtfull.

I really don't know what people are complaining about, she outlines EXACTLY what she wants on the syllabus and within the first day. There is a lot of busy work (the journal) but it is insanely easy and redundant, and takes 5 minutes out of your day. Pop quizzes, but in my instance it was the entire class working together to answer it, free points.
Professor Bodea knows exactly what she is talking about. This class is by no means easy, but I found that attending office hours and doing the textbook reading, I got along just fine.

Professor Bodea is amazing and cares a lot about the class topics. Class relies heavily on your own participation and willingness to engage in the topics being discussed. If you consider yourself a strong student who is willing to actively participate in discussion, attend every lecture, and do the readings you will have 0 issues in this class.

analysis.name: Ben Marley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 75 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Marley is the GOAT. The only people who give him low ratings are conservative corn balls who know they don't have an argument against him. He welcomes debate and additional viewpoints (it actually seems to really excite him lol) but you have to have some semblance of an idea of what you're talking about. He is also super kind and funny.

The class is structured around lectures with no direct notes and open ended discussions which are clearly opinionated and subjective, yet he grades you on definitions and clear answers even though the entire 1 hour and 50 mins is just ranting about why the world sucks. Exams are tough and you are given no study guide which he justifies for his sake

This class is hard because it's graded by a only few things, most of which are test-based. You HAVE to read the material and show up to every class or else you may miss something that will be on a quiz or an in-class activity. You may want to make a friend if you plan on skipping, which is important anyway because the exams are done with a partner.

You for sure have to attend the lectures to fully understand the material. Three essays made up for an "exam" portion. They were all pretty easy since you get a cheat sheet. He also replaces the lowest grades with the highest ones. He offers some in-class extra credit, so it's important to attend lecture. Overall, an annoying but fairly easy 4.0.

This guy makes no sense. Spent all the lecture times waffling about stuff not related to the assignments, has you do a reading and then doesn't discuss the reading in class, but then the assignments are about the reading? Some people liked it but not me

analysis.name: Carissa Buchholz
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor is prob my least favorite prof I've ever had. She is extremely difficult and frustrating to work with. She NEVER fully communicates what is going to be on the quizzes, to the point where the whole class banded together because we felt it wasn't fair, and she got defensive and said it would be our ONE quiz drop. (GLG 203)

She understands what she's lecturing about, but her skills are overshadowed by strict rules. Attendance VERY MANDATORY. If you miss the first minute of class you will lose attendance points. Only two iClicker drops a semester. Won't take doctors notes. The busywork is simple but pray you don't get sick twice. 93% to earn a 4.0. Difficult experience

Worst professor I've ever had. She couldn't care less about students, course is exam heavy and mandatory attendance. 1 min late you'll lose points, group projects every single day and tons of hw every week that u have to pay for. mandatory long study guides and the material will not be on the exam. please never take this class with her she's awful

Very clear what you need to do to succeed, need to get a 93 to get a 4. I got 100% on every non-exam and 88% on exams and got a 3.5. Prof is knowledgeable and does a good job of actually teaching the material and exams are quite easy, but the threshold for what is needed to get a 4 is very high, especially for a 200-level class. ATTENDENCE CRUCIAL

The class is very test heavy(exams make up 60% of your grade). Lots of in class assignments as well, but the assignments are only worth 0.71 points each. Homework is fairly easy(read and respond to articles). I personally think its ridiculous to make all assignments less than 2 points each and make the exams 50, but then again Im not a professor.

analysis.name: Bryan Ellis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Super time-consuming projects that are impossible to get 100%.
He uses iClicker + geo so get ready formind-numbing lectures, participation is 10%
Projects requiring teamwork CANNOT BE DONE ALONE so socialize or die (15%grade).
For the final, goodluck learning how to use OMEKA(super confusing)
If you took this class because you were late. Good Luck.

The class isn't that difficult but the professor is SO BORING. His lectures are mandatory, pointless, and so so slow, and he always takes random pauses when he talks that makes you want to bang your head on the wall.

DEI hire. Clueless. Class is a complete waste of time. After 4-5 weeks of listening to him, I decided to sit outside the classroom, with dozens of other students, check in for the attendance credit, then immediately leave. Rivals Jay Johnson for the worst hire in the history of Michigan State University.

First mistake, I ignored RMP. There is no way on EARTH that this man has any formal education or merit to be a professor. 1/4 of the lecture is him victimizing himself, 2/4 is him being passive aggressive, 3/4 is him complaining, 4/4 is his long pauses. If you try to ask for feedback on a project he will act like you insulted his family. Fire him.

Lazy and had to let dean officials know
- 3 heavy assignments and graded them after the semester ended but also made mandatory attendance (Leaving students in the dark, also does not follow his syllabus) 
- Emails go unanswered and excuses it for having 500 students 
- No rubrics for grading and doesn't discuss feedback 
Wont have a job in 5 years

analysis.name: Barb Gerber
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She is so nice and always cares for her students. She is very accessible outside of class and responds to emails very fast. She uses a sheet of paper to mark attendance and it does not matter if you are a couple minutes late to class. Would take her again and am convinced that she is the best teacher of this subject. Grade-100%
She is the best professor I had my freshman year. She is very caring and wants to see her students succeed. She is very flexible with grades.

Barb was a great professor. She really understands her students and the amount of work we have to do. We had deadlines on papers but she always moved them to about a week later. She took out a whole assignment because she thought we didnt have time. Definitely take her hybrid class, there was minimal work. And the papers were not even that long.

If you can, take the hybrid class because I do not see the point of going to a two hour writing class twice a week with the work that she assigns to us. Everything is very straight forward and most of her unit schedules are clear. I disliked how our assignments kept getting pushed back and things were graded late. She rarely responds to emails.

Barb SHOULD BE THE ONLY WRA PROFESSOR YOU TAKE! One time I forgot to turn in my paper by almost 3 weeks and she let it slide and gave me a full grade on it! Very nice and understanding, easy grader, easy assignments, easy 4.0, do not miss on the best opportunity to have the best WRA Professor in the world

analysis.name: Jan Brascamp
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Very chill professor, more than half way through the semester and we havent had a full length class yet. Answers questions through out lecture and his powerpoints are very well structured. You can tell he really cares about his students & is willing to help!

Brascamp is a very nice prof, and his class is pretty interesting. This class does have A LOT of content, so the exams can be a bit hard, but if you study, you will do fine. 60% of the lectures are mandatory for attending and there are studies you have to do, but they are easy. Exams are massive part of grade, so beware of that

This is one of the easiest psych classes I have ever taken. The professor doesn't go in-depth, which is nice since it keeps the exams really straightforward. It is test-heavy, but honestly, the questions are super easy if you actually study and understand the material. He uses PowerPoints, SO if you miss class, you can just read the slides.

I would recommend. Yes this class is hard and yes it is mainly lecture + exam-based. Brascamp's slides are amazing though, he is the first psych prof I've had that I genuinely learned from. He is passionate, gives tons of visuals, and explains very everything well. For exams, if you just study the slides and make a quizlet, u will be just fine.

His lectures are very heavy in content and he moves decently fast through the slides. He doesn't do much extra talking outside of what is written on the slide. Attendance isn't mandatory but you do get extra credit for going to class. There are no quizzes, just experiments and SONA. You'll definitely need to prepare for exams, but they're not bad.

analysis.name: Dustin Carnahan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor himslef was easy going however the classes were kind of boring. Majoritiy of the grade are speaches given in recitation. This is the major downside of this class becuase if you get stuck with a bad TA then you are kind of scrambling to lift your grade. Other than that the homework assignments, quizzes, and the final are pretty easy.

This professor was very easy going all semester and only had a lecture once a week. Even though he had a lecture once a week I will remember this class because his lectures were always very funny and he is a charasmatic guy and can tell he loves what he does. There is a quiz and reading assignment every week and then 4 speeches throughout semester!

Professor Carnahan is one of the best at MSU. He cares about what he teaches, even in an entry-level course. The lectures are mandatory with attendance, but he will do everything he can to keep you engaged. He uses the online McGraw Hill textbook for weekly readings and quizzes, but you should get an easy 3.5 as long as you try. Would take again.

Very interactive, make sure to participate in class/group discussions. Lots of group projects throughout the semester and does not give a lot of guidelines for how to do your work. However, his class was very helpful, and he gives useful constructive criticism.
While the lecture and actual professor was nice, the recitations with speeches and the weekly 50 question readings were very difficult. Having a harsh TA totally ruined my experience with this class.

analysis.name: Christian Houle
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Beware of surprise quiz. Make sure to read the readings before class because the quizzes are about them. Will drop two lowest ones. The total number of quizzes are unknown, completely up to him. No assignments. Lecture heavy and don't use slides but chalks and black board. Unless you are really into the topic, or else stay out of it.

I loved this class. The man is very passionate about what he is teaching, the notes are easy to follow. My only complaint is that you are only graded on attendance/participation and your midterm and final. The midterm and final are extensive, but he gives you the answers a week before the exams.

Our only grades in the class were attendance and 3 exams, which was rough. But, the exams are incredibly easy to do well on, as he provides all possible questions you can get and the answers come directly from readings and lectures. The lectures are comprehensive and easy to follow, and as long as you take notes you'll do well
Listen to me. This man is one of the nicest guys, but if you are not passionate about political science, save urself and don't take this class.

He's a really nice professor and loves what he teaches but he explains very quickly and to no fault of his own is just super monotone. The class is really boring, but he gives you the answers to all the questions on the exam and there's like a 8 page paper you have to write along with a research question presentation for the final part of class

analysis.name: Kathryn Clements
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Doesn't actually teach, just lightly reviews long textbook chapters that you have to pay nearly $100 to access and have to read weekly before the first lecture even begins. Wastes so much in-class time going over the "classroom rules"; we are adults and nobody came to this class to be told to wait until the bell rings to put their computer away.

The entire class is McGraw hill information on the exams (hardly any from lectures). In class she asks too many questions to students going off on large tangents and doesn't teach a clear lecture which makes it hard to follow. Also treats students like toddlers, were adults.

So rude, offers absolutely no support but acts like she wants the best for you. Gave a speech about how she made the test really hard but even then people did good, to her that wasn't "normal" so she proceeded to make it worse. She is very understanding towards students and is passionate about her teaching.

Tough grader, all readings are similar and not interesting. The class is tailored for specific people. It is unorganized and good luck getting a 4.0 on a paper. Her grading makes absolutely no sense. Would not wish this on my worst enemy

He overcomplicates everything and will take points away if you don't do work the way he wants it. He's actually a pretty nice guy, but worst prof I've ever had.

HORRIBLE class. He is a nice guy but I dont think teaching math is his thing. take calculus through university you get online exams.  if you don't want to watch your grade drop every week take it outside. really bad grading his teaching style is also wack.  the exam study guide doesn't correlate with the exam. Nice guy needs to consider changing su

Actually a horrendous professor (nice guy though). Ended up teaching myself everything because of it. Study guides do not help, and a very misleading grading system. You will have quizzes every week (on and off independent and group style) in recitation which is required. You cannot skip these quizzes without a doctor's note (same for exams).

Very passive-aggressive when asking questions, almost rude even. Not good at teaching and with the most unclear grading criteria possible. I legit couldn't see my percent grade all semester. Expect lots of meaningless group projects and busy work. Weekly quizzes that are pretty easy, but oftentimes hard to understand. Do not take.

I took LB 117 online, for the most part it was the same content as my high school calculus class but he either never elaborated on what he wanted us to do on the labs, or briefly went over what material he wanted us to turn in and always took so long to grade stuff. Overall horrible experience.

analysis.name: Nicholas Fields
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: This professor is such a fantastic, knowledgeable lecturer who has a deep passion for the topic. He explains these topics so well and with such excitement, it gets me excited to learn. I learned so much from this class without it being difficult.
Very nice guy that seems to care a lot about his students. Easy and fun class to take, good elective.

I took this class very last minute not knowing anything at all about music. One of the best professors I have ever had so far at MSU. He is really engaging and cares that you pass. Not even a music major! I am business but was my favorite class this semester.

He made the classroom a fun environment, and was very understanding near the end of the semester. His grading is very relaxed and the weekly assignment was a paragraph on whatever I wanted. I really enjoyed understanding music i'm gonna miss that guy

It wouldn't let me choose the correct course but I took IAH 241a with Professor Fields, which was Music and Society in the Modern World. I loved this class, especially for an IAH. Prof Fields has such a caring, kind demeanor about him which made me want to participate even more. Easy workload as well. This was the way an IAH course SHOULD be.

analysis.name: Francoise Gagnier
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: TAKE ANY OF FRANNY'S CLASSES!!! One of my first GD professors and definitely the best out of the others. Her course plan is extremely organized and straight-forward. Pushes you to be a better student and designer without the extra stress. 1000/10

One of if not the best professor I've had. She's nice and she gives great constructive feedback on your work. She's a really easy grader, and her lectures are concise and to the point.  She will happily take the entire class time to answer any questions. Highly recommend this professor, especially if you have ADHD. She will make your life easier.

I came into GD360 with no interest in graphic design, & left with a clear understanding of how to use Adobe programs as well as a curiosity for the medium as a whole. Franny is an amazing & compassionate educator, and as long as you apply yourself you should have no problem in her class. I wish I could have her as a prof for the rest of my degree.

Professor Francoise has been one of my favorite professors so far. She is caring, hardworking, and devoted to her students. She offers assistance whenever asked, and is always open to help out. I would 100% take a class from her again, and 100% recommend her to anyone taking Graphic Design courses!!!!!

analysis.name: Camille Fairbourn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Sweetest prof. ever, poor teaching style. Made many mistakes, not tech-savvy, wasted time. Wanted us to succeed, helpful 1-on-1 but should be teaching a smaller class. Content shouldn't have seemed so dificult to understand, I didn't like the way she overcomplicated things/underexplained things. She deserves to teach a subject she's better at

Professor Fairbourn genuinely made me like a math class! She is so kind and answers any questions! One homework assignment per week, 2.5% added to your final grade if you do all the EC, my TA was amazing and helped me understand the content. The Stats Learning Center is such an amazing resource if you're struggling, I highly recommend utilizing it!

Prof Fairborn seems like a sweet woman but it almost felt like she knew too much for a base level stats class, it got confusing at times. She goes through slides fast and it was hard to keep up during lectures. If you feel confident about math you'll be fine. If you struggle with math, then you may want to make sure you can find outside help.

Lectures and recitations were quite confusing. I thought that the lectures were a bit all over the place, and it was hard for me to follow what we were learning. She is really nice, but I do not think that she is the best teacher and I found the course difficult due to her teaching style.

I would try to take another professor. She makes the lectures very confusing, and most of the time, you are just doing examples and not actually learning the content, which made me have to learn it outside of class. Attendance is mandatory, but she offers make-up attendance questions at the beginning of the week. I wouldn't retake it.

analysis.name: Christopher Frilingos
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Frilingos created a phenomenal work enviorment for everyone in the class and anyone who does not rate him a 5 is trippin. Class was not mandatory but mostly all information was in class or online. The class was interesting on its own but if you can go to class a decent amount then you can easily 4.0, He will make you want to go to class.

Professor Frilingos is one of the most kind, compassionate professors I have ever had and he TRULY cares about your education! He will meet with you during office hours and make accommodations within reason for you to learn the best that you can. If you pay attention in class you should have no problem getting an A. Great guy all around.

Dr. Frilingos was by far my favorite professor that I have taken a non-animal science class with. He is extremely caring and respectful and truly wants to know what's going on with his students so he can help and support them along the way. I truly cannot sing his praises enough!

Frilingos is such a nice and knowledgeable man. He learned everyone's names (I've never had another professor do that before) and seems to genuinely care about his students and their success in the class. Although the class was a bit demanding at times (mostly with memorization), I ended up passing with an A.

This class was the best class I've taken, Professor Frilingos is caring and understanding, truly cares about his students and really loves what he's teaching. He's very open to other ideas that people may bring up in class and he leaves room for in class discussion. The best professor I've had!

analysis.name: Laura Genik
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr Genik is not only a great professor, but a great person. She genuinely cares about her students and is always willing to help if you reach out. The only thing I will say is to 4.0 this class you need a 94% which is pretty high.

There was a lecture part and a lab part, the lab was 2 days/week. The lab was not related to the lecture at all but both were pretty easy. On lecture tests she let us use 1 page front and back, for lab exams, we could use anything on the class website and old notes and homework. I learned a lot in the class, no book required.

While she can me annoying at times or seem condescending she really isn't. I got really get to know her and she was kind and always encouraged me to reach out for help. The class itself is so easy minus the matlab. 9 matlab hws, 2 quizzes, 3 reports, 3 self reflections and presentation every week.

The prerequisite for this course is calc I, yet we were expected to know and apply several calc II topics to the lecture homework. The labs are helpful but the lecture was a HUGE waste of time. Gives very tedious busy work. The exams are only 4 questions but you'll be lucky to get to the last problem. One of the worst profs I've had at MSU.

Your group is assigned by alphabet order, four people to a group. You can skip, but your attendance is noted. Handle yourself professionally, act in a professional manner, and you should be fine. Exams are 10 questions, all handwritten. Matlab has been added to the course so there is an exam that covers that. Final exam is a review game

analysis.name: Paul Gueye
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: TRUST NOBODY, did you guys eat lunch?, talk to your friends, measure with your forearm, this one is easy

Firstly, Paul was an amazing professor, him as an instructor, was a positive of the class. However, everything else was nothing but a headache. The class structure itself is completely terrible. Piazza feedback was MINIMAL. The lectures teach you what you need to know, but not HOW to apply it. I gave above a 4.0 effort but got a 3.5 instead.

Prof is hilarious and enthusiastic about teaching.  Lectures are abundant and do cover the material, but unfortunately, the organization of the class was awful.  Complete lack of online communication via Piazza and technical errors were common.  Enjoyed the teaching itself, but those issues make it hard to improve my rating.

Professor Gueye is great for teaching about the material, but not applying it to math at all. This class was a headache completely. Multiple problems with homework and quizzes. Not to mention there was very little interaction on piazza. Changed the quizzes format 3 different times.

Took PHY 183 P-Cubed with Professor Paul and nothing but good about him and the class. He cares for students and wants them to succeed. The class material is in-class problems that you solve with your group and the help of the ULA's. Homework is a big part of your grade so I would make sure to do well on them. Doing badly on exams isnt the end all.

analysis.name: Kimberly Fenn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 111 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Fenn teaches an informative and no-nonsense course. Some people refer to her as rude, but seeing as most of those people ask questions about things provided since the beginning of the semester I can understand her frustration. Lectures are not mandatory but you WONT pass this class without continued attendance and detailed notes. Would take again.

Super knowledgeable, probably more than most professors in her field. That being said, GO TO CLASS!! The exams are almost entirely based on class discussions. The lecture slides barely help and the textbook is basically your only option. The homework is chill but can take a very long time. Can be passive-aggressive if you ask dumb questions.

Professor Fenn was very thorough and outlined all expectations of the course. There is research included so be sure to get this done on time! Generous curves are provided and overall it is easy to succeed. Going to lectures are important and the course is test heavy---but there is a drop and a final will replace lowest score.

Dr. Fenn is a great lecturer and definitely knows her stuff. However, you can tell that she dislikes her life.  She is extremely hot and cold towards students. One moment she will be nice and the next she will lash out at you with no warning. I would avoid her if given the chance. Also expect rude emails and responses if you ask questions.

Make sure to attend class and take notes! The exams are based on lectures, the slides will not help you, attendance is not mandatory so don't let that tempt you. There is Inquisitive homework due every Friday night which is easy. Part of your grade is from research hours, and extra credit will be available to you.

analysis.name: Ritam Ganguly
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
If you want a professor who knows what he's teaching -- he's the guy. The class itself is hard, but he makes sure that everyone's questions are answered. It's essential that you reach out to him if you encounter any issues. Really helpful. 

Also, make sure you do his in-class activities -- he does notice if you are doing something else 😅.

This was Gangulys first semester teaching 260, and he did a pretty good job. He took feedback from students and got better as the semester went on.

Some advice is to watch the videos as they come out and take notes, attend the extra credit problem solving sessions, use the past exams to study for midterm/final. Do all the extra credit they offer.

This class is very difficult, however Ritam is extremely passionate about us learning. He was never content with just giving us the information, he was always ensuring we were actually learning from his lectures, and able to apply that material If things didn't go as planned he would be ready to adapt and accept feedback to improve the course.

He's tough but also caring. He will push you to the edge of your comfort zone but also will give you enough resources to help you. I just got off a zoom call with him at 12.45am, because I was facing difficulty solving a homework question. He was patient and caring, made sure I understood what I was doing. Grateful!
CSE 320's course topic is very difficult, but Prof. Ganguly tries his hardest to make it digestible. His exams are difficult, but he gives you so much to prepare for them that they seem much easier.

analysis.name: Gabriel  Ording
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Prof made the class very interesting, and the material was relatively engaging. The assignments due before class weren't overly difficult, and they all prepared me for the exams. While he provides lots of help prior to exams, the exams weren't the easiest and he ended up curving due to low scores throughout the class. He is overall a cool guy.

Gabe is the goat. One of the greatest men I've ever met and easily my favorite professor that I've had at MSU so far. I will admit it's a higher workload than a typical ISB class, but if you aren't a bum it's easy. Sit in the front and talk to him! You won't regret it!

Gabe is probably the best professor I've had at MSU so far. Attendance is tracked through half sheets which are things you write a bit of notes on and turn in, so bring a pencil and paper. There'll be around 3-5 online assignments per week. With the pop quizzes you can talk to your classmates so there's no need to worry about them.

He is an extremely harsh grader, if an assignment is even a minute late he gives you 50% on it. Also he doesn't tell anyone their grades, you have to talk to a TA who also never responds or emails, in person about assignment grades. You don't even get your full grade until the end so there's no way to make up anything.
Great man, terrible exams. the study guide he provides does not help at all. if you dont listen or pay attention, youre doomed. a lot that he talks about he doesnt put on the slides.

analysis.name: Sara Garnett
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Prof Garnett was kind and taught at a great pace. The class is straightforward; go to class, and you will pass. I recommend taking this class with a friend or making one in class for the in-class assignments. There is weekly homework except for the 3 exam weeks. It was simple and just extra practice class materials, mostly. Way better than BS161.

The professor is fine, but she assigns the most aggravating assignments ever. You will spend 2 hours redrawing THE EXACT SAME process with slight differences about 12+ times per assignment, on topics we were taught in middle school. We spent a month doing punnet squares. Dr.Garnett is a good professor, this class is a laughable waste of time.

There are a lot of assignments and areas to learn content and improve in this class. Prof Garnett explains topics very well in lecture and will be thorough enough for students to master content before exams. The exams were very straightforward and weekly homework assignments provided extra space to work on material taught in class.
Very solid professor, very understanding and caring.

I wasn't sure what to expect with this class being online, but Dr. Garnett made it really easy. Her lectures are easy to follow along with, but they are mandatory. The short in class activities each lecture and homework assignments definitely help prepare you for the exams. Dr. Garnett is also very kind and always responds to emails quickly. 10/10

analysis.name: Nick Haddad
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He will discuss things in lecture and tell us they won't be on the exam, so don't worry about remembering specifics.....he will then put said specifics on the exam! If you want to do well in this course, have a different professor. He is very knowledgeable about his field but some test questions are borderline impossible.

Dr. Haddad actually put my final class grade into the university incorrectly. So when my grades were finalized I tried reaching out to him using different means and I didn't hear from him for a while. He did respond eventually and had to file a form to fix my grade, which he did without apologizing for the error. It was very stressful for me.

Professor Haddad is very kind and knowledgeable about his field. His lectures are engaging because of how passionate he is. However, his exams are very difficult and very specific. Topics are explained well to be understood, but not to answer his own questions. I loved learning from him as a professional, but I didn't love taking the class.

His lectures were dry and unhelpful. Learned more from the text book, which wasn't much. Math heavy, but does not know how to teach math or allow calculators or note sheets. People in this class who put more effort than I did also complained about how his lectures and exams did not line up. Is a researcher who was forced to teach.

Although he is a sweet guy, his lectures were very boring and hard to pay attention to. The exams contained niche questions from lectures that would screw many of us over. He is not very accessible, but his TA was lovely. His lecturing is not interactive even in the slightest.

analysis.name: LaVelle Gipson-Tansil
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I usually don't write, but I had to this time. When someone asked for feedback, she said it was too much work. When I asked to make up a quiz the next week, she said yes, but when the it came she ignored all my chats and emails. When someone asked how to get graded, she put it in the chat for everyone to see. Grading is also bad.

Her grading system is ridiculous, she barely gives out extra credit even though on D2L there are lots of extra credit opportunities listed, and the lectures are so long me and several of my classmates fell asleep.

If you want to pass this class, here is a tip. when answering the field assignments, write essay length answers (or a large paragraph).

Worst professor at MSU. She will give you points to act like "you're earning points" until the final test comes around, you get a terrible grade for no reason. I don't understand her thought process when she grades. I think she just wants to give people a bad score for fun. Thought about switching my major a couple times, if that says anything!!

Terrible communicator. I emailed her so many times over the semester begging to get assignments graded that I completed on time, it took her months. She constantly posted wrong dates on D2L and never corrected them, leaving everyone so stressed. The class was very boring, she just reads the slides and then ends class with a NEVER ENDING WORKLOAD.

She had the dates on the quizzes wrong and I could not take them. She took a month to fix it and I had to take all the past quizzes in one day. She is a super harsh grader and does not explain why she took off points. She assigned about 15 pages of reading each week along with about 3 assignments a week plus a quiz. A 95% is 4.0 and a 70% is a 1.0.

analysis.name: Najib Hourani
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: ISS 320 consists of three exams, 1 extra credit opportunity for 5 points (usually a random lecture midday on a weekday) Exams are poorly written, shows up late, gives indirect answers to questions, and studying effectively is nearly impossible because he doesn't post slides. Goes on unrelated political rants. Exams are opinion-based, not an easy A.

Not enough grading opportunities to accurately judge a student's ability on the subject at hand. His lectures also follow a random pattern with no chance to study correctly due to his lack of assignments and withholding proper study materials, such as the slides.

I took ISS 320 with him. The class itself was about "urban planning." However, rarely have we talked about any cities, and when we did, we only talked about Arab cities. He has mentioned several times how he is from Lebannon and that is mostlyall we learned about: Lebannon and the Arab world. Only grades are 3 very difficult exams. I HATE HIM!

I took his class based on the reviews here and he is a good teacher but he is kind of a dictator in the class. He gives lots of reading and you have to be ready for class discussions, the first exam was easy but the ones after that were hard. All I can say is keep up with the readings and GO to class most of the exams are from class discussion.

I was so surprised to see negative reviews on Dr. Hourani. He was truly one of my favorite professors, and while his classes are reading heavy, he is very patient and understanding. If you make an effort and have open communication with him about any problems, you will do well in this class. He is engaging and makes the class feel connected.

analysis.name: Harish Sankaranarayanan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He uses tophat for attendance which you can do remotely. Overall if you attend lectures and recitation, understanding the content is really easy. Exams are a huge portion of the grade so you have to prepare for them. There's some extra credit built into the homework too.

Dr.H is funny, and stays after class to help people and is open to it. I asked to talk with him because I missed due to illness and he said no, thought that was weird but otherwise chill and communicating through email. I failed the class but I'd def take Dr.H again!

He was a great stats professor. If you go to recitation and go to class everyday, you will do great! One thing that annoyed me was him letting people go early which was super distracting to people like me who stayed all of class. Overall, super easy math requirement with only 3 exams and a lot of extra credit offered to bump your grade 2.5%.

Going to class is important because its easy to fall behind. Lots of extra credit. If you show up to lectures and recitations and do your homework and extra credit you will be fine. Tough grader however, Would not round me up .2 to next highest grade which was frustrating but like i said there is a lot of extra credit opportunities getting me close

Dr. H was a very nice and friendly man, but I felt like his lectures were too fast paced and at times he didn't fully explain the material. I would go to study for exams and would teach myself the whole exam material the week before the test. The content was not difficult it just took time to learn. There are many resources to get help such as SLC.

analysis.name: Joseph Hefner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, Doctor Hefner is AMAZING. If you do your homework, study, and go to lecture there is no way you would not be able to 4.0 this class. Also, just be honest with him he is so accommodating. He enjoys what he does and he loves teaching/talking to the class. The only way to fail this class is on your end, he wants you to succeed. TRUST ME.

(ANP441) Dr. Hefner was an amazing prof. Took the class for an Hbio selective and loved it! He's very understanding, caring, and easy to reach. Gave pretty clear study guides before the exams and lots of extra credit! I hadn't taken an anp class before and had no issues. Go to lecture and study the bones/ their characteristics and you can 4.0!

Teaches anthropology and made it fun! Exams are a little difficult but if you study and go through the study guide as well as some of the topics/practice questions from the smartbook you will do well. It is more lecture heavy but the content taught was not boring because he didnt make it boring.

His class was very interesting, and he was a really great professor overall. Make sure you go to every class; he gives extra credit, which lets you skip the final at the end. However, his exams are worth a lot, so I recommend taking many notes during his lectures and reading the book.
He was a very chill professor. He just requires attendance to do well as the lectures aren't typically posted. If you go to class you can easily 4.0.

analysis.name: Valerie Hedges
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: So kind and easy to reach through email. Wants everyone to succeed, and easy to 4.0 if you come to class and watch the lecture videos. She is very knowledgeable and helpful if you have questions. She makes this class run very well and it is not a class I ever worry about. Lockdown exams with no camera too and other assignments boosting your grade.

The flipped classroom style isn't for me, but Prof. Hedges was great. Her assignments are very interesting, and you can attend classes in-person OR online (Zoom). Do the study guides, keep up with assignments, and learn the content well- you will get a 4.0. One tip: Make sure you have a good grasp of the material. Tests are application-heavy.

Dr. Hedges was amazing. This class was super helpful to my learning and it was relatively easy to get a good grade as long as you did the assignments and understood how to do the exams. The class is hybrid which is nice if you can't make it. Be sure to do the in-class assignments and weekly quizzes and you will be able to 4.0 this course.

Dr. Hedges is very willing to work with you, and she provides a lot of course materials for you to understand the material. I didn't do too well, but looking back on it, this is only because I was stressed with many other difficult classes. Dr. Hedges gives amazing feedback, make sure to attend class and office hours!!

best professor ive had in all my 3 years. i have never learned as difficult information and actually understood it as quickly as i have in this class due to the way this class is formatted. i got the highest grades on everything without having to study once.

analysis.name: Kathleen Hoag
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Pretty standard freshmen seminar class for BLD students. Attendance is mandatory but the class meets once a week for 50 minutes so it isn't super demanding. I honestly did not buy the books but instead read them online but if you miss a reading it is not a big deal. The exam is not difficult, and neither is the class. She keeps it real.

This course was very test heavy but as long as you study the Learning Objectives you will pass very helpful for questions but the sheer intensity of so much content can make the course difficult if you don't invest enough time into the course which is stressed on by the professor. She seems to love the field and constantly updating the class.

It is graded on case studies and section quizzes. To be quite honest, focus well on the learning objectives and it will be fine. Some of the material is difficult, but many of the facilitators were helpful and so was Dr. Hoag. study well and you will be fine.

Dr. Hoag is a good professor at heart, but she heavily relies on you to do your part as a student. If you are looking into graduate school, she does help prepare you. She is not easy whatsoever and there are times where you may feel frustrated, but she does it out of good intent of making you into a smarter and more dilligent student overall.
She's definitely strict, but I enjoyed this class and thought she did a great job teaching.

analysis.name: George Harnick
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy! The class was very easy, and there were only 4 assignments the whole time. Guys, please laugh at his joke of the day it makes me sad when people don't! Kinda quirky, but a very passionate teacher and someone who would help you in the future in a heartbeat.
Such an amazing professor! Genuinely made every lecture so engaging and enjoyable. He is so funny and goes out of his way to accommodate and help students, could not recommend him enough!!

My favorite professor by far! He truly cares, adds humor to keep lectures engaging, makes students comfortable asking questions, and is always responsive to emails, even if you're a former student. He truly helped me love the class and want to be there and engaged. You have to write your name on a piece of paper when you go, but it's not mandatory.

George is one of my absolute favorite professors. Super engaging with the students and genuinely cares about his students' learning. You'll have to study for his exams but nothing too difficult. Also a little bit of homework but totally managable
He is the best. He is so nice and funny. He genuinely cared about each student. The class was so easy too.

analysis.name: Sadam Issa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Sadam is one of the best teachers at Michigan State. Arabic is a difficult language to learn, but his teaching methods are unmatched. Be sure to do the homework and required readings, he will be sure to tell you he's disappointed if you do not. Super caring guy, and attendance matters to him the most.

Would definitely take another one of his classes!
his new hst 150 is based off a 1,000 page book about capitalism. not what i expected for "global history".

Keith is one of my favorite professors at MSU. He teaches some of the best history classes I have taken here and he makes it very easy to pass. As long as you do the readings and watch the lectures you will pass. All the tests are in class and written essays but you get to have your readings/notes with you.

Wonderful professor, perhaps the best teacher I've had personally. Proffessor Charles is down to earth, approachable, and deeply passionate. Accordingly, it is very clear he cares alot about his students learning expierence and he is very careful in how he presents his information to not give a wrong impression. Extremely respectable guy. 5/5

Considering this was a level 100 course, it was super difficult to get a 4.0 in and I am an honors student. The TA did legitimately all of the grading and it was all written assignments. Your grades are not in d2l so you have to calculate everything yourself.

analysis.name: Lee Penyak
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For a normal IAH requirement this class was insane. I spent most of my free time on this homework. Sometimes the homework did not relate to class content at all and everything was graded by AI so he couldn't explain why sometimes you would get a lower grade. His lectures would go in circles and test questions were just so specific and picky.

Dr. Penyak was delightful and you can see how much passion he has for this class through his lectures. He grades generally easy and while there is a lot of information to memorize for the tests, the tests themselves are very easy to pass and he applies a generous curve to each exam. His love for history makes the course very engaging.
dr. penyak was amazing!! when i didn't do so good on the first exam, he reached out to me first and invited me to office hours. he is really good at keeping the class engaged, too.
dr. penyak was amazing. when i didn't do so good on the first exam, he reached out first and invited me to office hours. his lectures kept me engaged, too.

Very interesting class, Professor is very knowledgeable on Mexican history with personal connections. Daily discussion posts that once you understand what he wants are easy to get good grades on. The tests aren't too hard, he also gave an extra credit. I would definitely take a class with him again.

analysis.name: Rachael Lund
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Rachael Lund is a great professor.  The calculus program at MSU is super difficult and the exams sometimes seem nearly impossible.  Rachael makes everything very clear and doesn't move on until everyone seems to understand the material.  I am not even a math person and I could follow everything going on.

GREAT PROFESSOR! This course was online and organized well. Everything was super easy to locate in D2L and help was easily accessible outside of class. You're given ample time to complete assignments, but I personally used an assignment tracker spreadsheet to help. Easy to excel in this class if you follow the guidance and manage your time well!

great professor! very organized d2l page that is easy to access and check off. it can be a lot considering the amount of videos and other assignments for the week like webwork ($50-55 for the semester), snapshots, and projects, but everything is set up monday and due the next wednesday which is great and lets me work on other things! no final exam!

great asynch class with very organized d2l that made it really easy to keep track of work. decent amount of work due every week and a half, but its manageble. my only complaint is some of the "tech tasks" and "investigations" were so unnecessarily long and arduous it got really annoying.

This class reminded me so much of the same way a high school class was like where the teacher actually helped you understand. But overall, the professor was very involved even though it was an online class they always provided office hours, so they did want you to succeed and pass but still understand the material that was being taught.

analysis.name: Russell Lucas
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Lucas is extremely knowledgeable and clearly cares about supporting his students and their learning. He prioritizes methodology and the analytical process in his teaching, in addition to subject matter. The low reviews are just because of his tough grading, but if you are able to write coherently and support an argument you will do fine.
If you ask him a question, he will riddle the answer and make everything unclear. This was my hardest class at MSU so far, and I do not recommend taking this course.
Does not accept late work under any circumstances even if they're valid. Teaches humanities but is so far into academia that he's lost touch of real life situations.

I found his way of lecturing to be very confusing and unclear but that's okay because he's usually not the one lecturing. It's pretty much impossible to 4.0 this class. And although you should go to class to get information for your essays you could fake it without going. Go at the end in case he does a take home final like he did for us.

Professor Lucas is a cool guy, funny (if you like dad jokes). I didn't actually have him for 202, but he was my recitation professor for 201. The average recitation was him briefly mentioning the lecture and/or readings from the previous day, and putting us in small groups to write any questions on the board. Never answered them fully, little lazy.

analysis.name: Laura Markham
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Had 10:40-12:10. Prep work due the day before class, but she has an issue if you turn it in the night before, so points off. She will talk until 11:40 about the in-class assignment, but won't open it till she's done explaining, even tho directions are in the doc, so you will go home with hours of homework(she likes to hear herself talk).

Honestly terrible professor, she spends 1 hour and a half yapping about literally nothing then gives us barely any time to complete the lab and lets us out 30 minutes after the class has ended. One of the strictest graders every, if its not her way its the highway. You will flop an ICLA for misspelling one word. never take this proffesor.

Wastes the entire class overexplaining instructions then gives you 10 minutes to complete 2 hours worth of work you end up having to do at home. Only professor here that doesn't want you to succeed. Do not take this class.

analysis.name: Krystyna Kijewska
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kijewska is a tricky little bugger. She is the sweetest human ever but is simply not fit to teach this class. She is a little feisty and appears to not enjoy her job very much. The exams are very difficult and don't even reflect a lot of what we have learned. I would not take her as a teacher again, but she seems like a lovely individual!

Finish the ALEKS 100% before the deadline and the class should be a decently easy pass. Not super accommodating past the allotted absences so save them for emergencies. Lectures were actually helpful and I highly recommend going, even if you don't have to. If you survived AP Chem, it's basically a guaranteed 2.0. Chemistry is awful, she's great!

She posts Lecture Slide videos so if you need to review these are very helpful, Do your ALEKS as soon as possible! She seems snarky at times,sometimes she'll be like "I can't answer that, but a TA can." with a sarcastic smile. This can be frustrating. She also has an accent that isn't too hard to understand but definitely has you listening closer.

(Taken Spring 2023) 

Good lecturer, can sometimes go a little fast but is very nice with clear explanations. Her exams are easy to score high on if you follow along with the material intently. The people who scored poorly didn't study well or didn't care to set time aside to actually learn the material.

In the lectures it seems so easy and simple to understand, and I feel confident I have a grasp on the material. When i get into the exam, it's like it was written for a completely different class. The fact that this class also isn't curved when students tend to get like a 50% on the tests is beyond annoying. Also barely posts any study material.

analysis.name: Matthew Pauly
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: openly admitted we were going to skip things he felt were over taught because he finds them boring and would rather teach about his favorite parts of ww2. we only receive 4 grades 3 exams with vague prompts that require exact citations from 500+ pages of readings and participation.  please take another class and don't ruin a semester.

This was HST 344 Causes and Conflicts of WW2 but he said the European conflicts are over taught and decided to spend almost the entire class talking about  the USSR. we were assigned 100+ pages of reading most weeks and he refused to post his slides. this class is just his personal project and not close to the course description offered by MSU. if you enjoy hearing about the glory of the Soviet Union this is the class for you. if you want to learn about the rest of the war find another professor. graded on 3 exams and participation only.
He does not know how to lecture, and goes on many tangents. never taking a class with him again.

This is definitely one of the most difficult classes I have taken at Michigan State, it was HST 344: History of the Soviet Union. There is no textbook, instead it is 3 autobiographies that you are expected to read and integrate into the three essays, 6-7 pgs each, that are written in place of exams. Difficult class with a difficult structure.

analysis.name: Robert Laduca

LaDuca is a Lyman Briggs teacher and this was his first time teaching regular CEM 251. He teaches material fast and doesn't explain things in detail. If you don't naturally excel at chemistry, be prepared to teach yourself a lot of the material. He has messed up teaching us a few concepts and had to have T.A.s correct him which was very concerning.

Its hard to respect someone when they dont show respect towards you. Dr. L has a huge ego. He rushes through lectures as well as personal questions about the material-super uncomfortable. He also connects his lectures together very poorly, making his teaching extremely confusing. Each lecture seems like he is throwing random information at us.

Date of writing 03/30/26. I had Prof. Laduca last semester for LB 171 and he's been my favorite professor I've had. Write the practice exam on your cheat sheet, he tends to follow it almost 1 for 1. Class is structured extremely well, he's very accommodating, and just a fun person to know. His class is not hard, and he teaches the material well.
Gives female students suspicious deference. Thinks he's the life of the party, not as serious as he should be.

analysis.name: Vernon Miller
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
