review_highlights.comment: I would not recommend this course to anyone. The professor dosen't express the lectures enough and he will call on you even if your hand is not up. The exams are nothing like the "study sheet" that they provide and the course is extremely hard to navigate. Not to mention a big group project that has no substance to it. Don't take this course.

This class is an elective but is treated like a mandatory requirement. The tests and recitations are unnecessarily hard and there is no guidance by Professor Miller. He stumbles upon his words and expects you to read 35-40 pages of articles. The course is VERY poorly structured and includes multiple "suprise quizzes" during lecture.

Professor Vernon Miller is very unorganized. The course itself is very confusing and the lectures are unncessarily long. Attendance is required in recitation and each time missed is a point deduction. The TA's are not helpful and the workload is extremely hard for an elective. Do not take this class.

This class sucks. It is organized so poorly the recitations are horrible almost 2 hours of just listening to the same stuff talked about in lecture. huge group project that you get no time in class or anything to work on, it makes no sense that this is a group project because you do independent interviews. The lectures are so boring no no just no

He was okay overall, but the class often felt hard to follow. Lectures could get off track, and it wasn't always clear what we were supposed to be learning. This made studying for exams a bit confusing since they didn't always match what we focused on in class.

analysis.name: Thomas Nikolai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Nice, easy-going guy who you can tell really enjoys the content. No additional materials needed besides the posted lectures. My one warning is that the class isn't a slam-dunk 4.0 like the name would make you think, and the 3 unit tests + final (although they're open note) will sometimes touch on some of the more obscure points from lectures.

I took this along with World of Turf and I actually prefer this class over that one. The topics were interesting, the lectures were engaging and humorous (occasionally), and the professor actually cares for his students. Throughout the semester, he would give us so many updates/reminders. 4 total exams (final included) and 1 is dropped!

I recommend that everyone take this class! It's such a good class when you just need a few extra credits but don't want something difficult. Your grade is entirely based off of quizzes and tests but as long as you look over the lectures they are super easy. He makes the class very enjoyable and writes the nicest emails every week!

Honestly, an amazing professor. He's fully online and just has quizzes throughout the week that you have like a month to complete. I didn't even have to take the final because he only makes you keep 3 of the exams out of the 4. Also a really funny guy.

Great professor and a great class. Surprisingly interesting, and the professor is very nice and wants his students to do good. Despite being fully online, the class is well organized and easy to keep up with as well. Definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Paul Nelson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Nelson is an AMAZING professor that made this class super enjoyable. The grading for this class is weird but it's forgiving and the rubric for what you need to get 100% is always given to you. Despite this being an online class, he always tried to make it interactive and would do engaging activities rather than lecture us. 11/10 professor!!!!

I wouldn't take this class again. This capstone class is not very helpful in my opinion. The labor based grading system is very flawed as well. If you have to take this class, good luck. Also be prepared for tons of busy work every week, including the week of spring break.

One of those classes where you have many different assignments each worth like 1 point. Grading system is submitted to not so if you leave anything out/make a mistake you automatically get 50% on it. It felt like a lazy way to grade assignments since there were so many. Mostly projects and discussions- no tests. Grace period for due dates was nice.

Good professor. Bald professor. Interacts with students. Project based class: One group project and on individual project. Weekly quizzes. Interesting grading system, but there are extra credit opportunities.

analysis.name: Seven Mattes
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 133 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mattes was very nice and always excited to teach her class. Three group projects throughout the course, online exams including the final (no lockdown browser), mandatory attendance through tophat, and weekly surveys, quizzes, and prompts due every Friday. She was a very nice professor, just a little heavy on the workload.

This class was very manageable there was a discussion post due every week as well as a survey and a take home quiz, but overall the course load really wasn't bad. Her midterms, which she calls VDKs, were take home and online which was nice. You can tell she really is passionate about what teaches and seems very friendly.

Dr. Seven is a great professor, you can tell she is very passionate about teaching which makes her very likable. the assignments are super easy, but there is a significant amount of group work in this course. also most friday classes are cancelled for group work/exam purposes which is great

Dr. Seven is a nice person. However, she states that you will get 4 attendance drops, or full points back for 4 days, then only gives you the average across the days. If you miss 4 high point days, you only get about half your points back. She does not understand how this is unfair and it almost cost me my grade. Does not appear to read emails.

Seven is an amazing professor!! I greatly appreciated how she formatted the class. The course is structured in an organized fashion, and there are only 3 (open-note) exams. Assignments are very easy. There are a few group projects, but they are not difficult. I really recommend her if you want a great learning experience and an easy 4.0!

analysis.name: Stephanie Nawyn
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Nawyn's lectures. She's funny and explains terms/theories well. She has online open note exams, weekly readings, and iclicker quizzes, but they're fairly easy if you read the textbook and pay attention in class. Would 100% recommend taking SOC 100 with her!

All exams are open note/book, super easy class overall and hard not to 4.0! Lectures can be long/boring, she tends to get off task. The sweetest professor-intelligent, understanding, down to earth, absolutely hilarious. She wants everyone to succeed. I wish I could get coffee with her. Couldn't recommend enough!

Such a wonderful professor to have. She is educated, thoughtful, passionate, and caring to her students. She truly does care, and you can just tell. There were five exams, with the final, and one can be dropped. All are open note, and most were taken online, with an in-person option. No reason not to take a class with such a wonderful person :)

I love Prof Nawyn. There are iclicker questions and daily quizzes but they are easy as long as you do the readings which are a little long but its fine. Inquisitives were annoying but easy points. Very fun and followable lectures, shes funny here and there too. Very accommodating and there are many points in the class. Easy exams w a note card.

This is the easiest class I have taken. The lectures are important to go to for extra credit, lecture points and for exam material. There is so much extra credit given that I had 20 points of extra credit over the maximum points available in the class. You get a cheat sheet on the test and the beginning of lecture quizzes are just vocab.

analysis.name: Nicole Mccleese
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: McCleese only gave out 5 assignments the whole semester.  She takes attendance randomly so just attend even though it is boring af. Her lessons are so boring, playing minesweeper is more entertaining. She reads everything off of a slideshow, (which that is NOT posted to D2L).

Slow grades (no grades entered more than halfway through the semester), and the course topic is just not what the class is described as. If you want to learn more about Chilean politics, def take this course, but if you're looking for reading writing by women, this isn't it.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. I was expecting the course to relate to the description MSU put out, but she put an "indigenous food studies" twist to it. Lectures consist of her reading slides in a monotone voice. She gives us useless assingments and hasn't graded anything the entire semester (less than a month left). Stay away.

Very careless about student feedback or incidents. Took random attendance for the first month as a scare tactic, then suddenly stopped, nobody knows when she will take attendance next. If you are absent, she gives 0 grace to your situation regardless of how serious. She has a temper, and petty mannerisms. There's not much work she gives out.

This professor graded everything a week before the course ended. An okay instructor who oddly made the class about food culture. Assignments were easy ten-minute tasks, with only five total grades, so submit on time. Attendance wasn't taken, so skipping didn't matter. Clear grading, but never replied to emails.

analysis.name: Nathan Haut
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: GIVE THIS MAN A RAISE!!! Content & exams are seriously tough, but most of the grade comes from pre class & in class assignments & the project. Show up every day and you'll do great. Dr Haut is an amazing & chill guy who TRULY cares about his students (more than any prof I've ever had). I highly recommend him and getting to know him in this course!

so nice & genuine! really thorough w answering questions, i had a great experience w this class even as someone that doesn't like cs :) one thing is that the ML unit is quite hard, and it's common to not finish the in-class activities (although they are graded for completion). the exams are lowkey rough but they're not heavily weighted.

Anyone who rates him poorly probably never asked him a content question. He will sit with you and help you through your work. His explanations are clear and he is very thorough in his descriptions of the content. Very kind and engaging guy.
Super smart guy. Will give you high-quality detailed advice so make sure you pay attention.
Super hardass over a 2 hundred level course.

analysis.name: Nicholas Ovenhouse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the best math professors I've had. His lectures are very clear and simple making them not hard to follow along. His office hours were the main reason I got A's on the tests so I highly recommend going to them if you ever need help on the content or just for review before a test. He is always very kind and helpful whenever you talk to him.

Calc 3 is one of the hardest classes I've taken at Michigan State, but the main difference I vastly prefer it over Calc 2 is because of Professor Ovenhouse. His lectures were always super detailed and he always went over good examples, which prepared you really well for homework and exams. 10/10.
He was good at explaining tough concepts. I didn't get the best grade because I missed some lectures towards the end but every time I attended I was able to understand the concepts, very nice guy.
He is really good and the class in really exam heavy but as long as you come to lecture and understand the material the class is light.

Nick is a great teacher. He obviously loves his subject and wants his students to do well. He's very organized and will answer any questions you have in a manner that benefits you as a student. He'll go over homework assignments to make sure you can complete them. The only downside is Lab Day - you'll have to work in groups on a large worksheet.

analysis.name: Carmen Octavio
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: DO.NOT.TAKE.HER. Has no clear instructions and its a teach your own class. This is based off of homework and says it is based off completion when it is truly based on correctness.  She says you get three excused absences, but only marks participation as grading, so basically you can not miss a single class. I advise you drop the class if signed up

She is VERY picky when it comes to grading. Post-reading assignments will most likely be the lower grades you get in the class, because if you don't answer the questions in the way she wants, she will dock points. Somewhat recommend? It's not an easy 4.0, but if it fits your schedule, then why not.

Very direct and can have an attitude. Classes consist of mostly answering HW questions, which wasn't helpful as little time was left for lecture slides. Grading is REALLY tough and instructions can be unclear. However, HW is a big part of your grade which can cover up a bad exam. Very accessible outside class and helpful feedback.
Seems like a nice person, but I find the class to be mind-numbing. Expect to learn the material on your own time because the whole class time is taken up reviewing the homework from the day before.

This professor does not help you learn anything. She instead uses her time to send multiple emails out to students accusing them of using AI. Multiple people have now dropped the course due to fears of them receiving an academic dishonesty report, even if they didn't use AI... Adding to that, her D2L is not set up correctly. Do NOT TAKE HER !!!!!!!

analysis.name: Sebnem Onsay
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

Def NOT a 3 credit workload, more like 5 credits.

One of the nicest professors I have had, very helpful and knowledgeable. Not a good teacher though, lectures are hard to sit through and lecture slides are 100+ slides long every day making it almost impossible to study them or use them for projects.

Class was poorly structured with project quizzes usually happening 1-2 weeks after the project was due and quiz questions being generally confusing. But it wasn't that difficult, so it's fine. I don't appreciate the exams being outside of scheduled lecture times.

Bro she a GOAT. The course is chill, a lot of working but if you just see her videos and then go to lecture you'll be fine. She understands you got stuff going. She chill and tbh you can really vibe with her if you enjoy DSA like she does. Also she always looking for TAs so if you wanna be one just participate and make yourself known

Onsay was good. You can tell she cared about students doing well in the course and would always give side notes on what's expected in interviews and in your internships/jobs. The flipped-learning style of this class was not the best and there are far too many lectures with most lectures being insanely long. Overall, a very useful class.

analysis.name: Olufunmbi Elemo

review_highlights.comment:
MC377: Culture, Politics, and Postcolonialism: Profiling Sub-Saharan Africa
Here's the tea: Elemo is VERY supportive in providing resources and suggestions for final projects and large essays. Has engaging lectures and values class participation. Communication is key, highly recommend attending office hours. E-K is a great prof for this subject.

I had Professor Elemo for MC 201 and am currently taking her MC 492 class. She does an excellent job explaining complex readings and breaking them down clearly. She is thoughtful, supportive, and genuinely cares about her students' success.

Professor Elemo's truly one of my favorite JMC professors. I had some medical issues towards the end of the semester and she was extremely understanding when it came to my absences (unlike some other professors). She's truly passionate about what she's teaching and talking to her about class material is extremely beneficial. Highly recommend!

I had her for MC 201. Though I didn't like her class my freshman year, I realized she's actually an amazing professor in MC325! She has amazing lectures, helpful during office hours, and overall a very understanding professor if you show up. Attendance is very important but you're allowed four absences which is much more than other professors.

Contrary to popular belief, she's a very good prof. Her tone may be condescending at times, but she teaches well and has clear expectations. She is a tough grader but provides good advice. Just take her feedback into account and go to office hours if you're struggling and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: Orlando Hawkins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: My favorite JMC prof I've had thus far, he creates a comfy environment. I used to be so nervous to join discussions, but I was good to share my takes in this class. If you're a Straussian, you may not enjoy the critical readings so much, but there will be ample opportunity to interpret and grapple with the canonical texts. Participating is key!

Professor Hawkins is brand new to JMC/PTCD, but he is a truly great teacher. He really impressed me, and he did not shy away from tough topics, and fairly presented all the reasonable angles in this class, which is a pretty controversial class. I Highly, HIGHLY reccomend taking classes with him.

analysis.name: Osvaldo Hernandez

review_highlights.comment: You think that you understand the material, you study the study guides he gives you, then you get the exam and are mind blown because it is nothing like you expected! Such a nice professor!!! You also can tell how much he loves teaching this. Made class interesting enough for people who don't like science. Group projects that weren't awful although some days were more boring than others. Mandatory attendance but he usually lets us go early.

The TAs teach the course. I've never even met the main professor. If you get a good TA, then you will get a good grade. Luckily, mine was amazing!

In class assignments you can do from home, lectures are SO hard to sit through. three exams that were all taken online outside of class, not proctored. I would recommend to others for integrative studies requirement. very easy coursework that takes less than 10 mins. not a lot of homework at all

analysis.name: Oren Ziv

Awful class. For 98% of people it is a required class that is so obnoxiously hard. analysis.name: Peter Thompson

Cares about his curriculum and his students. highly recommend taking!

Incredible professor and super interesting class. Heavily focused on readings and discussions, but you can complete them whenever you get a chance and still get credit. Super fun guy and the lectures were interesting, engaging, and I never wanted to skip. Exams are open note, and there's only one essay assignment. I recommend this class to everyone

This class was truly fascinating and could not have been made better. Although the readings were sometimes a lot, Dr. Thompson was very lenient and allowed us to make up missed discussions on our own time without penalty. I couldn't recommend this class more, regardless of your major.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Truley cares about the students. Has thought provoking assignments and interesting field trips. Lectures can be mundane, but they rarely are and take up a small portion of the class. Could not recommend his class enough.

Dr Thompson is an incredible professor. His lectures are super interesting, and his assignments and field trips are really fun and interactive. He is also extremely understanding and cares about the well being of his students above all, and is just an amazing instructor overall. I would 100% take this class again!

analysis.name: Melissa Wurtzel O'shea
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: i took pls120 and she was great! she's an attorney herself! attendance is mandatory!!! there's lots of reading + case briefs at first but you get used to them. 2 exams and a group project you have to ask and answer questions on. she lets you use notes on exams but they are handwritten so i had to rush a bit. highly recommend!

Professor O'Shea is an amazing professor. She is so passionate about law and really understands what she is teaching. She offeres extra credit, and in the start of the semester there was a lot of homework that was heavily dependent on the reading. Attendance is mandatory but she typically lets us out a few minutes early so it makes up for it.

LOVED this class. At the start of the semester it was very daunting but once you understand the formula of how to write for her class you will be set. Very kind and knowledgeable professor, I will take another class with her in a heartbeat. This class is supposed to act as law school prep, so keep that in mind when considering taking 321.

This is an easy class, it is NOT a political science class. It is strictly law. She is a fair grader and its easy to pass the class. No one assignment will deck your grade. She is dramatic but it is an easy class to pass. You don't have to go to class but I would recommend it.

Professor O'Shea is a GREAT teacher, she makes law very fun and interesting even if it is only an intro class. There is ALOT of reading, there aren't any textbooks required for the course but for the first half of the semester you will have to read cases. Only two exams and a project, both open note. Easy A!!!

analysis.name: Patrick Arnold
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Arnold is one of the most caring professors you will have at msu. They are very understanding and want you to succeed. There is an assignment due every other week that only takes about 30 minutes or less to do and 2 campus event reflections. As long as you complete your work the best you can, they will give you a 100!

Super nice and actually cares for students. The class itself is super easy and has discussion questions every other week which is really nice. Grading is super lenient and the assignments and readings are easy. Sometimes you do not even half to read the book to answer the discussion questions. Honors option is also easy.

i took this as an elective, easiest class ever. prof arnold is very sweet and such a nice person. this class requires little to no work. there's 1 online assignment a week that normally took ab 10-20 mins. u have to go to 2 events of ur choice during the semester. no tests/final. love prof arnold!!!

Professor Arnold is a great teacher and you can tell they genuinely care about their students. It's really easy to get a 4.0 as long as you complete the assignments. Probably the easiest class I've ever taken and doing the assignment each week didn't take much time.

Professor Arnolds class was amazing. I felt that the material was good and easy to understand, and they were extremely understanding for every single assignment that there was. There were also no exams! Overall I really liked this class.

analysis.name: lLina Qu

review_highlights.comment: easy and super interesting class that only meets once a week. Just gotta go to class and raise your hand 6 times in a semester for full participation so easy again. Readings are through perusall which is annoying but again if you can't read 20 pages once a week you probably should not be in college. a few easy cooking assignments, great prof.

The class literally isn't that hard. Some of these reviews are just overreacting. That being said, I wouldn't take the class if you aren't into East Asia, which I feel like is pretty obvious already. There is only one lecture every week and one quiz every week with some projects and you need to participate 10 total times in class for the whole sem.

There is a weekly quiz on a movie and/or a reading every week which can be annoying. There are participation stickers and you need 10 to get 100%. Attendance is mandatory with two unexcused. Quizzes are not lock down. Has a midterm paper and final online presentation. Nice teacher, didn't have any problems.

Loved Dr. Qu! I'm honestly not sure why these reviews are so bad… her class is extremely easy. I got stuck with this class because it was the only IAH that fit into my schedule, however, I really enjoyed it. Class was only once a week and I actually found the lectures to be pretty interesting. Easy homework (quizzes) and midterm/final assignments.

Read the weekly course material and participate in class- the course is easy. People love to complain about everything. If you put effort into the essay portion of quiz you'll earn extra credit; I had no problems. 

I recommend this class to anyone genuinely interested in East Asia, b/c I enjoyed the material she provided. The lectures are boring.

Professor Qing is an exceptional, extremely caring professor. If you want to 4.0 the class, go to her office hours and do her honors option! She gives extra credit (unlike other JMC professors) and show your appreciation for her. Nevertheless, try your best and your work will be recognized.

Professor Qing is one of the sweetest and most understanding professors I have ever had, and she is very knowledgable on a variety of political science and IR topics. I appreciated that Professor Qing took the time to make sure we understood her lectures (she recognises that her accent is hard to understand). My biggest problem is that her guidelines for assignments are incredibly vague.

I love Dr. Qing! I really enjoyed her MC 201 course. She was very accessible outside of class and got to know us as people in addition to students. Her research is very interesting. She was a fair grader and attending office hours was really helpful. She is very sweet and I'm so glad to have developed a relationship with her. 100% recommend!

Very nice professor. Took the time to explain everything and in a way it made sense. A homework quiz attached with every chapter lecture, but she reviews all the questions in the videos and you get unlimited attempts. The exams were similar to the quizzes, overall easy class and great professor!

I am good with computer stuff so the class is a lot easier for me than my friends. Remember it's a finance class.

One of the most enjoyable classes. I went to the lectures sometimes just to cheer up. Whatever happened in the news/reality, she made relevant jokes and is super positive. I never know someone can make so many jokes about finance. I learn a lot about everything else in addition to finance.

Robby was hands-down the best professor I could ask for. He cracks jokes all the time and he really knows what he's doing. He's also very good at keeping the class engaged. I wish I could retake the class every semester.

analysis.name: Amy Pollock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor & very clear for those who may not understand chemistry well. Free book is a bonus. Very easy class. Participation and attendance required. Amy is amazing. She is a super kind and a cute lady. However, if you do not come to the lectures, you will fail. Class material is basic chem and Amy teaches it super well. She is very passionate and explains every thing in great detail. There are about 2 easy homeworks a week.  Overall, if you come to class and pay attention, you should pass.

Dr. Pollock is a great professor and one of the best I've had at MSU. If you actually pay attention to the lectures then you will be fine. She makes chemistry easy to understand and a 4.0 is not very hard to get.

She is hands down one of the best professors that I ever had. The lectures were very easy to follow, but to understand the posted slides, you most often had to attend lecture. The exams tested your knowledge, but if you go and get outside help the exams are a piece of cake - and you can get extra credit. I would highly recommend her as a professor.

You need to attend lecture to understand anything, and then outside of lecture you need to look at the slides and make sure you understand what is going on. Study... a lot. The exams are nothing like what's done in lecture or recitation so make sure you look at the practice exams before hand and make sure you know how to do everything on them.

analysis.name: Lolo Robison

Truly the best Prof I have had all of college- sees potential, passionate about projects, and incredibly hands on work! If you just show up and participate you will pass easily- she truly cares about the success of her students which is so refreshing.

Just take her courses, even for fun. Sometimes it can seem like a good amount of work but it is all so worth it and important info that will lead you to finding out more on your own. Her DEI course was great and very informative. LOVE her!!

This is my second class with Lolo, and she's great! My advice would be to participate actively in group discussions. She's great to have conversations with. You do most, if not all, work in groups but the work is easy
I loved Prof. Robison! She always let us out early, and the assignments were really interesting! The final is a group project, but it is very easy if you read the rubric.

analysis.name: Ronen Steinberg

Ronen is the coolest dude ever. He is so funny, and also quite attractive as well. His lectures are very interesting as well as his accent. Mr. Steinberg is an all-around great professor. He teaches tough topics with respect and passion. He truly cares about everyone and wants you to succeed, so take all the extra credit opportunities he gives you. Reading the textbook DEF helps, and being engaged in recitation is just locking it all in.

Prof Steinberg is my lord and savior. Funny guy. Certified history hater but he made it my favorite class of the semester. There are a few easy quizzes and bigger essays but 100/10 class hes amazing

stay away from this professor, he needs to retire.

One of if not my favorite classes and professor ever. This class (IAH 206, not english!) will stick with me for a long time and I'm so happy to have been able to take it. Dr Cho is so understanding and accommodating to her students. A truly wonderful person!

Great professor. Everything about the class was meant to be difficult, but he taught it in a very intuitive way. Fair grading, and easy to score if you study. Helpful, responds to questions fast and effectively on Piaza. Textbook not required but is extra credit.

He loves to advertise to his students, and will add ads for his own personal benefit to your homework assignments. If you show up loving drawing, you might hate it by the time he's done with you.

Extremely tolerant & patient & respectful. Decent lecturer. Keeps self-promotion of his work to a minimum but it's still very slightly annoying. D2L somewhat poorly organized. Projects take up a LOT of time, beware. Pretty good feedback on projects. Strange attendance policy. Most material probably could be independently learned from Scott McCloud

STA201: Loved this class. LOTS of work depending on how ambitious you are. Show up to class even if you don't have the project done. Chime in during discussions. It's always been a dream of mine to make comics and this class has let me do that. 
Btw you don't need the course pack if you're a digital artist. Ames lettering at most for one assignment

Honestly, it's the participation. As another rating said, if you are even 30 seconds late he will mark you absent. I was 1 minute late once, and I walked in and he had already started lecturing. He doesn't even wait for class to start to take role. The class is also focused heavily on time-management, but it's HIS time management. Not good for all.

He obviously knows what he's talking about, but does so in a way that is accessible and down-to-earth. If you're interested in exploring the comics medium or diving in to improve your work, the comics courses with Ryan Claytor are a great way to go. Workload is a bit demanding, but I've never experienced another class that made me feel so proud!

analysis.name: Claire Vallotton

review_highlights.comment: Honestly really disappointed in Dr V and course. I love my HDFS classes and was excited for this course, but the way it was delivered was atrocious. There were SO many guest lectures and I lost points on a paper due to my references not being found in the database (even though they were) she just didn't take the time to look. Very condescending.

Felt more like a personal therapy class for her to talk about things going on in her life and "how we would respond to it." Every paper we do has three separate due dates for references, 3 weeks in advance of the due date, which is extremely unnecessary. Tough grader on everything surrounding the papers, including finding scientific research. Avoid

Seems nice, kind of condescending. I was so excited to take this class until i realized it was not what i thought. So many long papers and she's a TOUGH GRADER! Random guest lectures constantly that (in my opinion) waste time. Random attendance so you never really know when you need to be there. Don't take if you can avoid.
Don't take if you can avoid. I get it's a parenting by class but it's all from her parenting perspective and I feel like very few lectures helped on the THREE 6 page papers. EXTREMELY tough grader

HDFS 414.... 3 papers- very detailed and had to use scientific evidence. I wouldn't take her again but it was fine. Some discussions in class. Papers were kinda hard and they SUCKED. Don't think it is just an easy A. Hard grader on essays

analysis.name: Claudia Vergara

review_highlights.comment: Class is very easy, but boring at times. Lectures are disorganized. No tests, no final. 1 assignment and home quiz a week. She grades tough sometimes, but you can have two drops per category. Be in class b/c there's in class work on random days and you can't make it up, you have to be there (that is the largest part of your grade minus the final).

Honestly, the class really isnt that bad. You just have to make sure that you are always checking D2L and keeping a planner. Her quizzes had no time limit and were fully open note. Yes, she is a tough grader, but once you learn how to write to her style it's relativly simple work. Just show up and put effort into the assigments and you will be ok

This woman will talk and talk forever about nonsense. Lectures and homework and exams do not match up at all. Gave me a 0 because I submitted the final in the wrong format. 0 in the CLASS mind you, and I did all the coursework and showed up. Take any other option because this woman will ruin your peace and gpa.

ISB at MSU with Dr. Vergara starts with two weeks of syllabus. No late work is accepted, even by 5 minutes. Weekly "preparations" feel pointless, graded by TAs/ULAs who look for keywords. ICA tasks are rushed, with just 25 minutes to complete. Grading feels unclear and strict.

I would give this professor a negative score if I could. This class is sooooo disorganized, she jumps all over the place and the class has no structure. Most of the work needs to be done on the weekends and they are graded harshly. You never know what to expect in class and be prepared to not have enough time to do anything!

analysis.name: Melanie Cooper

She doesn't write on slides so if you're rewatching lectures, you will be lost. Alex (hw site) was painful to get through and is worth 10%. Recitation helped for understanding content. You can find Textbook pdf online

Dr. Cooper is a caring and honest professor. She might be a bit blunt for some people but I think she's hilarious, She definitely does care about her students' learning too

Actually pay attention and take notes in lecture, take the 45 minutes to actually do BeSocratic activities, check your notes a few times a week and no reason to not get a 4.0

Professor Cooper made the class way harder than it should've been. She states the facts but doesn't teach the reasoning behind them. The tests weren't difficult because of the material, but because they were confusing and worded badly. Homework is assigned after every class but doesn't take very long. I'd recommend choosing any other professor.

This class was hard. I ended somehow with a 2.5 but had a 1.5 for most of the class. Never got above a 50% for the first 2 texts. Textbook is a waste it doesnt help. Homework is due before every class. There is iclicker for attendance but you can drop 2 and its not for accuracy. some people get this chem and some dont. I had many tears here

she mumbles into her microphone  while teaching new information as if the class knows it already and doesn't go into much detail about anything and has frequently started debating with students in the lecture hall about the wording on her questions. not approachable during office hours either

analysis.name: Michael  Cooperman

review_highlights.comment: LOVE prof cooperman! I had him my freshman year and he was amazing! He is super easy to work with and a great teacher!
A chill professor, let us always go early. The grading was very lenient. A few missed classes here and there didn't matter as long as you submitted the work. Highly recommend. Easy 4.0
Condescending but the class is not bad

analysis.name: Marcie Cowley

review_highlights.comment: She cancels class at least once a week with less than an hour warning. Did not seem interested in helping each student. Just read off slides word for word. Tests are online and open note. Only 3 attendance drops and she takes attendance twice per class.

Date of writing 03.30.26, exams are in-person and no longer open note. Exams are purely based on memorizing details from textbook and videos. Class is just about immigration despite other possible interpretations of the title. Does not test your understanding of the immigration situation, it tests your ability to memorize and spit information.
She was at most okay; she would cancel class less than an hour before it started (she did it at least once a week). There is a lot of group work  and a lot of reading but it is easy

She's definitely a talker and will not stop, but she is nice. The class is very easy, but it is two hours long and feels repetitive. You have to do two hours of community service every week. I liked the volunteering part, but going to class was boring. There is group work every class, attendance is mandatory, and most of your grade depends on it.

The class is really easy. When I took it, the class was only about European migration with a focus on the 2015 European migrant crisis. The class is interesting if you enjoy social studies. Exams are online, and you don't have to be in the class to take them. Every class, you will have attendance and a quiz of one question relating to the material.

analysis.name: Sheila Contreras

review_highlights.comment: Communication is key for this class. Professor Contreras is very understanding with her students and genuinely cares for them. She even asks students what she could do so they can better understand her class. Her class does involve lots of reading but she gives students enough time to do the assignments Most caring professor by far.

Prof Contreras is a caring professor who is readily available to her students if they need help, and my writing ability definitely improved in the class. However, she is somewhat unorganized, rambles, and the course theme didn't really feel very connected to me. Her teaching style will work better for some than others, and unfortunately not me.
She says attendance is mandatory, god forbid you don't participate in a lecture... it's 8am and the lady can't stick to one topic. Overall, don't recommend. I see why she got a low rating.

Take the other ratings with a grain of salt. I had her for IAH207H, and she was fantastic! She can ramble and seem unorganized at times, but she always gave good feedback on paper ideas and can definitely help if you're struggling! She genuinely cares for her students and has our best interests in mind.
The professor is wonderful, I just didn't always enjoy lecture.

analysis.name: Henry Cowan

review_highlights.comment: You can do fine on quizzes if you go to every lecture. Lecture slides are posted after class. I averaged a 98% on quizzes by going through the slides and typing everything up and reviewing it. Lectures are interesting. EC is available through SONA, or an essay. Very interesting topics discussed in class, and you can tell Prof Cowan is passionate.

I honestly liked him as a professor; he was very professional. But it's not open note now for quizzes and exams. I do very poorly on quizzes if I miss class, SO i really recommend going and taking notes from what he's talking about. Tip: definitely don't remember the material, and even less so how to apply it to the quizzes and exams.

Mr. Cowan was very professional and talked a lot during class. He said his exams were hard—and they were. Even though they were only 20 questions and open-note, I felt stressed due to limited time and space. I wish there were more interactive activities. Homework was light—just one weekly Achieve task.

He wants us to be challenged a little bit and writes the quizzes in a way that we would be stimulated. I loved the material and didn't mind it, and this was easily my favorite class this semester! The material is pretty clear. although it goes a little fast.

Prof. Cowan is a great guy and very professional. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I found that I would perform poorly on quizzes if I missed class. There are four quizzes with one drop, but even though they are open note, I got mediocre scores. Little to no homework, but make sure you study hard for the quizzes (they make up 40% of your grade).

analysis.name: Corrine Higley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: She's nice and approachable. In each class, you answer mandatory ICA questions from the slides with your table group as she lectures. Iclicker attendance. Group CER's. Practice exams are usually identical to the real ones, so fill your note sheet to the brim. The repettiveness can become boring, but bear through it, there's few absences allowed.

BEST PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD. She's extremely passionate about biology and it shines in her lectures. She's well rounded and cares about her students plus she's funny and adds memes to her slides! Whats not to love??? The exams are very similar to the practice exams and as long as you participate in class + complete ICA's, you are bound to succeed.

Grading criteria and concepts are relatively simple. Her lectures are good and she makes the materials simple to understand (no curve ball questions on exams). Exams are relatively straightforward and practice exams are almost identical to the actual exams. The assignments are collaborative. Only issue I have is that you need a 92% to get a 4.0

Overall good professor. Her lectures were engaging and she tried to make the class fun. The work was mildly difficult but she made it easier to understand. Not too sure about other BS162 professors, but she would be a good option if you need to take BS162.

Your lab group definitely makes a difference, and I was lucky mine worked well together. The professor was extremely nice and passionate, and she would give extensions if you needed and emailed her. Doing things with R was a little difficult, but she works through it with you. Going out to collect samples was SO fun too, I had a blast.

Very slow grader.

Wasn't a clear order/structure of the class (random assignments every week) but prob better in person? Some weeks were less work according to holidays/breaks. Overall decent but wouldn't take again.

Took online. Nice professor, answered emails quickly. The class was a module every week which was lectures, a open note quiz, and sometimes a case study which was longer writing quiz. One final exam, have not taken that yet. Overall easy class, and interesting material.

Pros: Easy content, extra credit, and professor is responsive if you need help
Cons: D2L page is very disorganized and lots of busywork

This was my second course with Dr. Eustice, but CSUS 200 was much more disorganized. The content is not difficult, you just have to pay close attention and there are lots of unnecessary assignments.

This professor was very... different. One of the homework assignments showed us how privileged some were than others and there was a quiz on how to apologize to people. It's super easy but there are assignments every week. I wouldn't recommend it but definitely not hard.

analysis.name: Cristina Schmitt

She is very disorganized and not the best at explain the content of the class. Her lectures are also not structured, making them hard to follow and understand. However, she did offer a lot of extra credit on the final (added up to 20% to midterm exam grade). Her intentions are there but her lack of organization makes the class difficult.

I will NEVER take this class with her again. Try to take this class in the spring with a different professor if you can. Lectures were unorganized and I lost points on the homework for problems she helped with. Make sure to go to the TAs instead (they grade them). D2L course was also never updated with lecture material, so you have to go to class.

The professor is a great person, BUT she was extremely disorganized. You have to go to class and take notes since nothing is posted online. If you miss class, then you will most definitely be behind. The overall grade in the class is determined only by harshly graded weekly homework assignments and 2 exams. Take this class with another professor!

analysis.name: Rene Crespin

review_highlights.comment: It isn't said anywhere, but you should definitely take EC420 before this class. So far it is very regression heavy. The slides are the worst part of the class. Poorly made, spelling and grammar errors everywhere. Midterm is coming up and it is so hard to study if you want to read the slides. To be fair, the subject is pretty interesting.

Class structure is well taught. Majority of the material is being able to read and interpret graphs, basic econometrics but not rigorous whatsoever. Professor is willing to meet if you are having issues, attendance is not worth much. Don't let the other reviews deter you this class is a much better option than other ec 400 classes.
Lectures are easy to understand, homework is pretty easy, takes attendance regularly.

Knows plenty about education economics but not how to teach. Would read off poorly made slides that he refused to even post on D2L which makes it incredibly hard to study. Had no clear learning goals or objectives for each unit so I didn't know what to learn. What is actually on exams or his in-class essay is a mystery and I often was blindsided.

review_highlights.comment: The class is taught by different guest lectures which is made clear in the beginning of the course. I really found this class to be interesting and enjoyed it thoroughly. Craig was honestly one of my favorite professors this semester. He truly knows his craft and lectures well. If you choose his class ensure you go to his office hours for participation. There's a lot of reading in this class however, participation in class discussions is highly encouraged but not forced. He is a hard grader however.

Professor Craig is a very good professor. He is quite anti-technology, so beware of that, but many of the PTCD faculty are. He is overall a great teacher though and makes himself very available. Not an easy professor, but if you pay attention in class and do most of the readings, you'll do just fine.

If you're a PTCD major this doesn't apply to you, as I am sure he is a great PTCD professor. Taking MC201 with him as a freshman was absolutely horrid. Very harsh grader. If you are someone who is not interested in political theory, and you were planning on taking him for any other type of class, don't.

analysis.name: Karenanna Creps

I highly suggest her for this class.

She lets you redo any assignment with a low grade even if it's from the beginning of the year. She makes learning fun and creative. Totally recommend her for Learning Through Drama.
Love her! Recommend 10/10 for the Learning through Drama class!! Easy to talk to:)

review_highlights.comment: Professor Crosson is the greatest thing to ever walk into a biology classroom. He is super nice and very eager to help students understand the material. The class is flipped, which takes some getting used to, but he always does a recap at the beginning of class, which is very helpful. Also he had a little texas accent so he is fun to listen to.

Dr. Crosson is probably the best BS 161 professor you can find at MSU, however, he only teaches every 2 years so be mindful when you are scheduling for this class. Every other BS 161 professor needed to be switched out in the middle of the semester except for him because he was actually knowledgable on the topic unlike the others as I hear it.

Dr. Crosson is a thorough professor and is good at what he does. He is very knowledgable in the content and is super caring/understanding! The book is required, but it does not really help that much and the main content is in the lectures/ICAS. Extra credit opportunities are offered for exams 1-3(1 point each). I recommend him!

BS 161 was a very difficult and consuming class, but Dr. Crosson and his TAs/UALs were phenomenal. Without them I would have failed this class without a doubt, but they did an amazing job of helping every student who needed it and explaining the why behind the processes. Dr. Crosson is truly a great professor, and I wish I could have him again.

Hard class, but great professor. You get used to the stupid schedule, but it's a flipped classroom, so you teach yourself everything, then recap with questions and examples in class. Lot's of homework and studying. Iclicker questions also count for a grade. Crosson is great at answering questions in depth, so try and you'll be fine.

analysis.name: William Crank

review_highlights.comment: I appreciate that he used his own experiences in the business in lectures, as that gave applications and context to lectures. However, that's how he gave lectures. Almost purely through his own experiences. You have so few opportunities to earn a grade, so every little thing matters. This course caused so much stress. If you can, avoid his classes.

Yea so William Crank got cranky and made me stay after class to give me a lecture on being on time. I also was surprised by how much he bragged. He would  brag about things way off topic all time. If you tell him you know something he might argue you or brag he is better at it.

Honestly, he was not a bad professor. He does really care about the future of his students and constantly would bring up opportunities and opened himself up to help guide students which I thought was really nice. The exams are a little hard but if you show up to class you will understand whats going on. The group project was pretty easy too.

I am currently taking PR 305 with him this class is easily the worst class I have taken at msu He does not make any assignment clear every assignment he will not provide exact details of what he wants us to include. Crank is a piece of work. Easily one of the worst professors on campus, but is a God in his own mind. Never take this man, as he will make your semester 10x harder than it needs to be. analysis.name: Robert Cummiskey
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Love this guy. I had a mental health crisis halfway through the semester and went from being there everyday to missing most classes. He was super understanding and had no problem accommodating me through that time. Also a super light grader as long as you put effort in. I would happily take this course again if I had to, great GPA boost.

I loved Dr. Bob! He made a gen-ed writing class very enjoyable. There are only 5 essays, or "projects" that you have to complete over the course of the semester, and as long as you stick to the rubric you will be fine. On top of being hilarious, he also gave me really good feedback that I could put towards my future essays.

Bob is a great and funny guy. The class he teaches is pretty easy. As long as you show effort, you'll get a good grade. The only problem is that he talks a lot. His lectures can go on a very long time because he goes on long tangents and repeats himself often. Other than that he's very helpful and nice. His lectures can drag but he's still great.

If you want a professor who genuinely cares about you, Mr. Cummiskey is your guy. He is super considerate and is willing to work with you if you communicate. Great teacher, would definitely recommend for WRA 101.

Prof. Cummiskey is very casual and a great guy to interact with. If you show up to class and participate, he'll remember you and be more likely to help out when you need it. Class was very easy, mostly documentaries with writing projects throughout the semester. Very easy class to take for the IAH credit, plus it's a very fascinating subject.

analysis.name: Curtis VanDonkelaar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Curtis is an entertaining professor who cares a lot about his students, loves his job, and grades easily. That being said, he also assigns a myriad of homework at times, but he is very flexible with due dates. His lectures often have groupwork, and many assignments are peer review, so beware if that is not up your alley.

He is a really nice guy and if you participate a little he is super willing to help you and be accommodating. He does not put grades in which sucks but he gives you a lot of time for each project and gives really good feedback. Just show up and do the work and you'll be fine. He says attendance is mandatory but you can miss 2-3 times.

Doesn't put in grades until last minute BUT it's a fair and good amount of workload, if you miss one class you're fine. You get 4 absences through the semester. He's very very very caring and understanding and wants you to learn and understand course material. He is an amazing professor and very passionate of what he teaches.

He was an amazing professor, but my only complaint is that he did not grade any assignments until after finals, so I worried a bit about how he grades. All the assignments are very clear to complete and he allows you to turn in assignments late. Not a harsh grader, got a 4.0 in the class.

Really nice and caring guy. He just wants you to show up and participate. Do the work and you'll get a 4.0. Overall super easy class with an even better professor. Highly recommend taking this course with him.

analysis.name: Everardo Cuevas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He claimed that my paper was done by ai, which it wasn't and gave me a horrible grade. There was nothing I could do cause it was the end of the year. He is ALWAYS late to class and will cancel it 10 min before it starts when everyone is already in the classroom. Unprofessional and expects a lot when he doesn't hold himself to the same standards.

Dr. Eve was an amazing professor that taught a very well structured English class. He was very caring to all students and grades pretty leniently. Do your work when assigned and you should be able to easily get a 4.0.

Professor Cuevas is an excellent teacher. He's fun, helpful, and genuinely passionate about teaching — something that's increasingly rare these days. A professor who actively engages with students and truly wants them to learn already goes above and beyond. Show up to class, put effort into your projects/peer reviews and you'll 4.0 this course.

Professor Cuevas is truly one of the best professors I have had at MSU. He is so laid back and understanding. Communication is key in his class and despite any sense of intimidation you may have, there is no way to fail unless you are simply not even trying. Always always communicate with Cuevas and your results in this course will be great!

I really recommend Eve, he is a great guy along with an amazing teacher. Attendance is required for this class by the school, and the class is graded based on 5 projects/attendance. You should get a 4.0 if you show up and put in effort into the projects/online posts. The only thing that sucks is the grading scale used by the school - 94% is a 3.5

Professor Currie's lectures are long and have a lot of confusing info, I found it easier to not attend and study it at my own pace. However, she gives few extra credit points for attendance. The material is interesting. The class would be so much better with a different professor though. Great person. Not great at explaining things. Some student have done really well. I am not one of those students. The material is confusing and she confuses me more with the way she explains things. Overall, this class sucks but you can do well in it.

His lectures were interesting and easy to follow. You can tell he enjoys teaching. Attendance is required and he uses iclicker to check the grades. The test study guides he makes are important. If you can do those, you can do the exam.  He has a generous extra credit policy.

Professor Cuncic is very passionate about physics. He is helpful and responsive to feedback. He is exactly what I would hope for from a physics professor at MSU. I am happy with how things turned out in this course and I would take any course with him teaching.

Katz was the best professor I have had so far. She is very passionate about philosophy and is very clear. She manages to be very interactive in such a big lecture. The study guide and the exams are close to identical, so make sure that you stay on top of that and ATTEND CLASS. You definitely won't pass if you don't come to lecture and take notes.

She's a good professor; knows exactly what she's talking about. However, if you plan on doing at least 5-10 hours of reading a week, this would be the class for you. The reading blocks were very excessive (4 days before class, having 30 pages to read. And 2 days in between classes, having 60 pages to read).

She was a very kind professor. Her lectures were very clear, and she made philosophy pretty interesting for a stem major. you can tell she is very passionate about Philosophy, and she's very experienced. Exams are completely based on the study guides, so if you don't get an A that's on you. Loved her class, highly recommend for IAH

analysis.name: Emily Pomeranz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very sweet & passionate about what she teaches. If I ever had questions outside of class she was very helpful & timely over email. If you show up to class & engage you should do well, the slides dont always have all the info.Use office hours to your advantage (for any prof). I just wish there would've been a clear study guide for exams.

Enjoyed this class a lot. I think a lot of people don't understand how important HD is. She was disorganized at times but in general had informative lectures. Lots of readings but I got by without doing most of them. Exams were a little hard to study for but I found that I was pretty prepared just from taking notes and attending
You will do well if you go to class and engage with the content. Dr. Pomeranz is a good professor and clarifies any confusion if you ask. I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it!

Dr. Pomeranz completely lost the class a month in, maybe 25% came. Lectures are extremely boring and disorganized, you gain absolutely nothing from going. It's supposed to be a writing class, but 2 exams are worth 45% of the grade, in which she gives zero study references. She does not respect your time either and rambles about nonsense. STAY AWAY!

analysis.name: Emily Elliott
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: For HST 201 our final was a 15 page paper. Prof. Elliott is very nice and caring, she gives great feedback on assignments preparing for the paper. She is very easy to get in contact with and responds to emails pretty quickly. She also made it clear that she is always willing to help and care for her students. Very passionate about her job.

Basically half your grade is one paper, but you spent most of the semester just working on it, so it was ok. Elliott is a great speaker, and the class was very entertaining. She would make us work in groups during class sometimes, which was fine but there were some students that made it suck. Clearly very passionate about Russian history.

Prof. Elliot was a very understanding proffessor. She did go through lectures pretty quickly but she does post them at the end of units, but just paying attention helps. There are no tests or quizzes, just 3/4 major writing assignments. She is really timely in replies and you can tell she really enjoys teaching this class. Recitations are also fun!

So, shes a little rude, and she goes through notes a lot faster than some people are prepared for. But, Her assignments are very easy and clearly detailed. 4 assignments including the final. Compared to MSU's other ISS 210 course this one is MUCH easier. The other having almost weekly tests and quizzes.

Professor Elliot lectures every class and then recitation is set up to talk through her lectures and the assigned readings for the week, I found it to be easy because she posts the power points but I would definitely suggest still going to her lectures. There are pop reading quizzes and very few assignments, so try hard and meet the deadlines.
